facts.text: Singapore's hawker culture was added to UNESCO's intangible heritage list on 16 December 2020.
Hawker Culture in Singapore was Singapore's first inscription on UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage list.
Singapore ratified UNESCO's 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage on 22 February 2018.
UNESCO's evaluation body recommended the hawker culture nomination for inscription on 16 November 2020.
Hawker culture's UNESCO inscription was announced at the 15th session of the intergovernmental committee.
Singapore's hawker culture nomination involved NEA, NHB and the Federation of Merchants' Associations.
Singapore's UNESCO hawker culture nomination file was submitted in March 2019.

facts.text: NEWater is high-grade recycled water produced from treated used water.
PUB set up a team to test water-reclamation membrane technology in 1998.
A NEWater demonstration plant commissioned in 2000 could produce 10,000 cubic metres per day.
NEWater was introduced to the Singapore public at the National Day Parade on 9 August 2002.
The first two NEWater plants opened at Bedok and Kranji in 2003.
NEWater purification includes microfiltration or ultrafiltration.
Reverse osmosis is the second stage in PUB's NEWater treatment process.
Ultraviolet disinfection is the third stage in PUB's NEWater treatment process.
NEWater is used primarily for industrial processes and air-conditioning cooling.
During dry periods, Singapore adds NEWater to reservoirs for indirect potable use.
Singapore's SingSpring Desalination Plant opened in 2005.
The Singapore River clean-up was launched in 1977.
